prompt.context: Our client is a dominant spare parts distributor in Europe and they want to enter the US market at end of this year. Our client collects spare parts from the manufacturers and distributes it further within the region. The client has approached Bain to determine the US market size for next year.
prompt.question: What is the US market size for spare parts for next year?

clarifying_info.q: What types of vehicles should we focus on?
clarifying_info.a: Focus on the passenger car market for this case.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client distribute all types of spare parts?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — the client has strong relationships with all spare parts manufacturers in the USA and distributes all possible spare parts in the market.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the client's customers / distribution channels?
clarifying_info.a: The client distributes spare parts to retailers, car manufacturers, workshops, etc.
The question asks for the overall market size; the presence of competitors does not affect the total market size.

exhibits.title: Total number of passenger vehicles in US
exhibits.shows: A table breaking down the total number of US household passenger vehicles by income category, showing the number of households, cars per household, and total cars per category for High, Medium, and Low income groups.

data.note: Non-household vehicles (taxis, limos, government cars, rental cars) must also be considered.

framework: Number of passenger vehicles in US
Frequency of maintenance per vehicle per year
Number of spare parts used per vehicle per maintenance
(Optional) Number of repair workshops in US as a sense-check

questions.prompt: How many passenger vehicles do you think there are in the US?
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment households by income level, estimate cars per household per segment, sum household vehicles, then add non-household vehicles (taxis, limos, government, rentals). Key assumptions: US population 350M, 3.5 members per household = 100M households; High income = 20% of households (4 cars each), Medium = 50% (2 cars each), Low = 30% (1 car each).

math.setup: Total household cars = (High HH cars) + (Medium HH cars) + (Low HH cars) + non-household vehicles
steps: Add non-household vehicles (taxis, limos, government, rental cars) = 40M

questions.prompt: We conducted a survey of repair workshops and obtained the following data. Calculate the total US spare parts market size: # spare parts per vehicle per maintenance = 1; frequency of maintenance per year = 1.5; average price per spare part = $10.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the full market sizing equation: Total Market Size = # vehicles * # spare parts per vehicle per maintenance * frequency of maintenance * price per spare part. All inputs are provided; the test is clean multiplication and correct unit tracking.

math.setup: Total Market Size = # vehicles * # spare parts per vehicle per maintenance * frequency of maintenance * $ per spare part

brainstorming.prompt: If you were told that you need to estimate the market size using three more variables (beyond the number of vehicles), what would those be? Write down the complete equation. Then describe how you would go about collecting that information/data.

categories.name: Three additional variables
ideas: Number of spare parts per vehicle per maintenance
Complete equation: Total Market Size = # vehicles * # spare parts per vehicle per maintenance * frequency of maintenance * $ per spare part

categories.name: Data collection approach
ideas: There are 50 states in the US with varying demographics; interview repair workshops across each city since they hold data on # spare parts per vehicle per year and average price per spare part
With ~40,000 cities and towns in the US, surveying repair workshops across 10,000 cities/towns provides a good representative sample
Frequency of maintenance can be estimated from personal experience (e.g., taking a car to the workshop twice a year) and validated across the surveyed sample

recommendation: The total US spare parts market size is estimated at $3.75B USD
This is calculated based on 250M passenger vehicles and data gathered from repair workshops across the country (1 spare part per maintenance, 1.5 maintenances per year, $10 per spare part)
Even capturing 5% market share in year one implies revenues of ~$187.5M — a compelling entry opportunity
risks: Total market size alone does not indicate achievable market share or competitive dynamics
Upfront investment and ongoing cost structure for US entry have not been assessed
Analysis currently excludes non-passenger vehicles (trucks, motorcycles, etc.), which may represent additional opportunity
next_steps: Assess how much market share the client can realistically capture in year one and in subsequent years
Model profits and return-on-investment for the US market entry
Extend the analysis to include non-passenger vehicles to capture the full addressable market
